contribution.value: Introduces PIQA, a multiple-choice benchmark for physical commonsense reasoning where humans reach 95% but large pretrained models (GPT, BERT, RoBERTa) plateau near 77%.

ev.quote: we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical **Interaction: Question Answering** or **PIQA** . Though humans find the dataset easy (95% accuracy), large pretrained models struggle (\sim77%).
We introduce a new dataset, **PIQA** \triangle, for benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding. The underlying task is multiple choice question answering

data_size.value: Over 16,000 training QA pairs, ~2K development, ~3K test; goals average 7.8 words, solutions average 21.3 words; >3.7M lexical tokens in training

ev.quote: In total our dataset is comprised of over 16,000 training QA pairs with an additional \sim2K and \sim3k held out for development and testing, respectively. Our goals, as tokenized by Spacy
**a**. **GPT** (Radford et al. 2018) is a model that processes text left-to-right, and was pretrained using a language modeling objective. We use the original 124M parameter GPT model.
**b.** **BERT** (Devlin et al. 2019) is a model that process text bidirectionally, and thus was pretrained using a special masked language modeling objective. We use BERT-Large with 340M parameters.
training hyperparameters. We use RoBERTa-Large, which has 355M parameters.

ev.quote: | FAIR RoBERTa | 355M | 79.2 | 77.1 |

key_results.value: Human performance reaches 94.9% validation accuracy, ~18 points above RoBERTa
BERT-Large reaches 67.1% validation / 66.8% test, GPT 70.9% / 69.2% on PIQA
Roughly 20-point absolute gap between best model and human performance on PIQA

We introduce a new dataset, **PIQA** \triangle, for benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding. The underlying task is multiple choice question answering
we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical **Interaction: Question Answering** or **PIQA**

strengths.value: Targets reporting bias by using instructables.com to seed annotators with atypical everyday tasks, flattening the object distribution.

ev.quote: To address this, and flatten the distribution of referenced objects (see Figure 5), we prompt the annotations with links to instructables.

strengths.value: Applies AFLite to remove stylistic artifacts that artificially inflate model accuracy on prior NLI benchmarks.

ev.quote: we use AFLite (Sakaguchi et al. 2020) to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples from the data, which have been shown to artificially inflate model performance on previous NLI benchmarks

strengths.value: Provides a detailed error analysis showing RoBERTa fails on relations like before, after, top, bottom near chance level.

ev.section: PIQA as a diagnostic for physical understanding
ev.quote: RoBERTa struggles to understand certain highly flexible relations. In particular, Figure[ 7](#page-5-0) highlights the difficulty of correctly answering questions that differ by the words 'before,' 'after', 'top', and 'bottom': RoBERTa performs nearly at chance

strengths.value: Establishes a clear ~20-point human-model gap, giving the field a measurable target for physical commonsense progress.

ev.quote: The results show a significant gap between model and human performance, of roughly 20 absolute points.

weaknesses.value: Finetuning was unstable for some configurations, with some runs landing near chance accuracy especially for BERT.

ev.quote: we found that finetuning was often unstable with some hyperparameter configurations leading to validation performance around chance, particularly for BERT.

weaknesses.value: Examples were truncated at 150 tokens, affecting roughly 1% of the data.

ev.quote: we used the transformers library and truncated examples at 150 tokens, which affects 1% of the data.

weaknesses.value: Some "mistakes" in development errors were actually correct but required a web search to verify.

ev.quote: Manual inspection of the development errors show that some "mistakes" are actually correct but required a websearch to verify.

weaknesses.value: Validation removed correct examples needing expert domain knowledge, narrowing the scope of "commonsense" the dataset captures.

ev.quote: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data. This often meant that correct examples were removed that required expert level knowledge of a domain

limitations.value: All data collected in English only, limiting cross-lingual physical reasoning study.

ev.quote: https://spacy.io-all data was collected in English.

limitations.value: Only three pretrained text models tested (GPT, BERT, RoBERTa); no multimodal or larger LLM baselines reported.

ev.quote: we consider the following three largescale pretrained transformer models

limitations.value: Benchmark targets text-only models; does not evaluate embodied or vision-grounded systems despite citing them.

ev.quote: these examples suggest that physical understanding – particularly involving novel combinations of common objects – challenges models that were pretrained on text only.

limitations.value: Test labels are held out, so all reported test accuracy depends on a leaderboard rather than open evaluation.

ev.quote: an additional \sim2K and \sim3k held out for development and testing, respectively.

future_work_stated.value: Build language tools that capture enough physical knowledge to bootstrap robotic-language applications.

ev.quote: Key to our research aims in this work is helping to build language tools which capture enough physical knowledge to speed up the bootstrapping of robotic-language applications.

future_work_stated.value: Build language representations that capture knowledge traditionally only seen or experienced.

ev.quote: Our goal with PIQA is to provide insight and a benchmark for progress towards language representations that capture knowledge traditionally only seen or experienced

future_work_stated.value: Encourage research into learning physical commonsense from interaction with the world rather than text alone.

ev.quote: Philosophically, knowledge should be learned from interaction with the world to eventually be communicated with language.
